# 30-Day Reading Challenge: June 1–30, 2026

A balanced 30-day plan for **6 books total**: **2 fantasy, 2 nonfiction, 2 mystery**. It fits your reading window of **25 minutes on weekdays** and **60 minutes on weekends**, with built-in buffer time for catch-up.

## Reading Mix and Weekly Rhythm

**Plan structure**
- **Fantasy:** one book in Week 1, one in Week 3
- **Nonfiction:** one book in Week 2, one in Week 4
- **Mystery:** one book in Week 1, one in Week 4

**Pacing target**
- Weekdays: aim for **10–20 pages** or **1 chapter**
- Weekends: aim for **30–60 pages** or **2–3 chapters**
- Reserve the final 2–3 days as **flex days** for catch-up or finishing

## 30-Day Reading Plan

| Date Range | Focus | Reading Goal | Book Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jun 1–3 | Start strong | 1–2 chapters per day | Fantasy #1 |
| Jun 4–6 | Keep momentum | 1 chapter/day | Mystery #1 |
| Jun 7 | Weekend push | 2–3 chapters | Fantasy #1 |
| Jun 8–10 | Finish first half of book | 1–2 chapters/day | Fantasy #1 |
| Jun 11–13 | Switch pace | 1 chapter/day | Nonfiction #1 |
| Jun 14–15 | Longer weekend sessions | 2–3 chapters/day | Nonfiction #1 |
| Jun 16–17 | Steady progress | 1 chapter/day | Nonfiction #1 |
| Jun 18–20 | Reset and re-energize | 1 chapter/day | Mystery #1 or buffer |
| Jun 21–22 | Weekend recovery | Catch-up + finish any lagging book | Buffer |
| Jun 23–24 | New start | 1 chapter/day | Fantasy #2 |
| Jun 25–27 | Deepen the read | 1–2 chapters/day | Fantasy #2 |
| Jun 28 | Weekend finish line | 2–3 chapters | Fantasy #2 or Nonfiction #2 |
| Jun 29–30 | Close the challenge | Finish remaining book(s) | Nonfiction #2 + Mystery #2 |

## Suggested Book Order

| Slot | Genre | Reading Goal | Suggested Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| Book 1 | Fantasy | Fast-start, immersive | Jun 1–10 |
| Book 2 | Mystery | Shorter, momentum-friendly | Jun 4–10 |
| Book 3 | Nonfiction | Slower, reflective | Jun 11–17 |
| Book 4 | Fantasy | Mid-month reset | Jun 23–28 |
| Book 5 | Nonfiction | Finish strong | Jun 28–30 |
| Book 6 | Mystery | Short final read | Jun 29–30 |

## Pacing Tips That Make This Work

- **Use weekdays for consistency, weekends for depth.**
  Weekdays keep the habit alive; weekends are for longer chapters and catch-up.

- **Choose at least 2 shorter books.**
  A 200–280 page mystery or nonfiction title can keep the plan realistic.

- **Track by chapters, not just pages.**
  Chapters are easier to finish in a 25-minute block.

- **Stop mid-scene when possible.**
  Ending a session at a natural break makes it easier to restart tomorrow.

- **Keep one “easy-read” book available.**
  If a dense nonfiction title slows you down, switch to a faster mystery for a few days.

| Jun 10 | Nonfiction #1 | 25 |  |  |

## Missed-3-Days Recovery Plan

If you miss **3 days**, use this fallback without restarting the challenge:

- **Step 1: Drop the next planned book switch.**
  Stay with the current book until you regain momentum.

- **Step 2: Use the next weekend as a catch-up block.**
  Put **60 minutes on both Saturday and Sunday** toward the most behind book.

- **Step 3: Reduce the goal temporarily.**
  For 4–5 days, read only **10 pages on weekdays** and **25–30 pages on weekends**.

- **Step 4: Reorder for quick wins.**
  Move the shortest remaining mystery or nonfiction title earlier.

- **Step 5: Protect the streak, not perfection.**
  Finishing **5 books well** is better than forcing 6 with stress; if you’re behind near the end, use June 29–30 as finish-only days.
